items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce
items.summary: This update resolves critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities that could lead to arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, and security feature bypass. Adobe is not aware of any exploits in the wild for these issues.

items.title: Improper output encoding in webhooks leading to arbitrary code execution
items.summary: An unauthenticated, zero-interaction flaw in the webhooks component allows for arbitrary code execution due to improper output encoding. This is a critical vulnerability with a CVSS score of 10.0.

items.title: Unrestricted upload of dangerous file type
items.summary: This critical vulnerability allows attackers to upload malicious files, such as webshells, to the server due to unrestricted file upload capabilities. It has a CVSS score of 9.6.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization leading to security feature bypass
items.summary: An unauthenticated attacker can bypass security features on a live store due to an incorrect authorization vulnerability. This issue has a CVSS score of 8.6.

items.title: Unauthenticated PHP object injection in Mirasvit Cache Warmer
items.summary: Sansec discovered an unauthenticated PHP object injection vulnerability in Mirasvit Cache Warmer, a Magento extension. A crafted cookie on any storefront page can lead to remote code execution.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce
items.summary: This security update addresses multiple critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities, including issues that could lead to arbitrary code execution, arbitrary file system write, application denial-of-service, and security feature bypass.

items.title: Unauthenticated unrestricted file upload in Magento REST API
items.summary: A critical flaw in Magento's REST API allows unauthenticated attackers to upload executable files disguised as images. While Adobe fixed it in the 2.4.9 pre-release, no isolated patch was initially available for older production versions.
